title: 77 days with Jesus
description: A provisional course assembled from the supplied candidate readings.

weeks.title: Abiding in Christ
weeks.description: Begin with relationship and dependence rather than performance.
weeks.introduction: Begin with relationship and dependence rather than performance. This week, read slowly, bring your response to God in prayer, and consider one practical way to respond. These practices are a response to God’s grace, not a way to earn His love.

weeks.title: Scripture
weeks.description: Learn to receive, understand, remember, and respond to God’s Word.
weeks.introduction: Learn to receive, understand, remember, and respond to God’s Word. This week, read slowly, bring your response to God in prayer, and consider one practical way to respond. These practices are a response to God’s grace, not a way to earn His love.

weeks.description: Develop honest, trusting, and sustained conversation with God.
weeks.introduction: Develop honest, trusting, and sustained conversation with God. This week, read slowly, bring your response to God in prayer, and consider one practical way to respond. These practices are a response to God’s grace, not a way to earn His love.

weeks.introduction: Make room for repentance, changed thinking, and a different way of living. This week, read slowly, bring your response to God in prayer, and consider one practical way to respond. These practices are a response to God’s grace, not a way to earn His love.

weeks.introduction: Understand belonging to Christ as received grace rather than earned standing. This week, read slowly, bring your response to God in prayer, and consider one practical way to respond. These practices are a response to God’s grace, not a way to earn His love.

weeks.description: Practice love of God and neighbor in concrete, truthful ways.
weeks.introduction: Practice love of God and neighbor in concrete, truthful ways. This week, read slowly, bring your response to God in prayer, and consider one practical way to respond. These practices are a response to God’s grace, not a way to earn His love.

weeks.title: Service
weeks.description: Use your abilities and opportunities for another person’s good.
weeks.introduction: Use your abilities and opportunities for another person’s good. This week, read slowly, bring your response to God in prayer, and consider one practical way to respond. These practices are a response to God’s grace, not a way to earn His love.

weeks.title: Stewardship
weeks.description: Use time, attention, abilities, and resources responsibly before God.
weeks.introduction: Use time, attention, abilities, and resources responsibly before God. This week, read slowly, bring your response to God in prayer, and consider one practical way to respond. These practices are a response to God’s grace, not a way to earn His love.

weeks.description: Practice belonging, encouragement, and shared life in the body of Christ.
weeks.introduction: Practice belonging, encouragement, and shared life in the body of Christ. This week, read slowly, bring your response to God in prayer, and consider one practical way to respond. These practices are a response to God’s grace, not a way to earn His love.

weeks.title: Mission
weeks.description: Live and speak as a respectful witness to Jesus in ordinary settings.
weeks.introduction: Live and speak as a respectful witness to Jesus in ordinary settings. This week, read slowly, bring your response to God in prayer, and consider one practical way to respond. These practices are a response to God’s grace, not a way to earn His love.

weeks.title: Perseverance
weeks.description: Continue in faith beyond the end of these 77 days.
weeks.introduction: Continue in faith beyond the end of these 77 days. This week, read slowly, bring your response to God in prayer, and consider one practical way to respond. These practices are a response to God’s grace, not a way to earn His love.

days.title: Remain in Jesus
days.devotional: Jesus describes fruitful life as the life of a branch remaining in its vine. Receive His words and love before treating spiritual practices as a measure of your worth.
days.reflectionQuestion: Where are you trying to produce spiritual growth through effort alone rather than dependence on Jesus?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask Jesus to show you where you are trying to grow without remaining close to Him.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, I often try to carry everything myself. Teach me to remain in Your love and receive the life that comes from You. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Receive His rest
days.devotional: Jesus invites weary people to come to Him and learn from Him. His rest includes a new way of walking with a gentle Teacher.
days.reflectionQuestion: What does Jesus’ gentleness reveal about the way He receives your weariness?
days.prayerPrompt: Tell Jesus what is making you weary, and ask Him to teach you His gentle way.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, I bring You my weariness. Help me receive Your gentleness and learn to walk with You instead of carrying every burden alone. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Receive God’s care
days.devotional: The shepherd’s care accompanies the psalmist through danger as well as rest. Trust does not require pretending the valley is absent.
days.reflectionQuestion: Where do you need to receive God’s care rather than assume you must provide everything for yourself?
days.prayerPrompt: Name a place where you need the Shepherd’s care, especially if the way ahead feels uncertain.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord, You are my Shepherd. Help me receive Your care in places of rest and in the valleys I would rather avoid. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Trust the Shepherd
days.devotional: Jesus distinguishes His care from the self-interest of a hired hand. His willingness to give His life reveals the character of the One who calls you to follow.
days.reflectionQuestion: How does the Shepherd’s willingness to lay down His life affect your willingness to trust His leading?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask Jesus for help trusting the leading of the Shepherd who gives His life for His sheep.
days.writtenPrayer: Good Shepherd, thank You for loving Your sheep at such cost. Help me recognize Your care and follow You with growing trust. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Seek the bread of life
days.devotional: The crowd seeks bread, but Jesus directs their attention to Himself. Bring your needs to Him while considering what it means to receive Him as life itself.
days.reflectionQuestion: Are you seeking Jesus primarily for what He can provide, or for the life found in Him?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring your practical needs to Jesus, then ask Him to deepen your desire for life with Him.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, You know what I need. Help me seek You for who You are and receive the life You give. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Continue in Christ
days.devotional: Paul connects continuing in Christ with being rooted in Him and overflowing with gratitude. Growth builds on what Christ has done rather than replacing dependence with self-sufficiency.
days.reflectionQuestion: What would it mean to continue with Christ in the same dependence with which you first received Him?
days.prayerPrompt: Thank Christ for receiving you, and ask for help continuing in the same dependence today.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, root my life in You. Keep me from replacing trust with self-sufficiency, and let gratitude shape the way I live. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Seek His presence
days.devotional: The psalmist brings danger and desire into the same prayer. Seeking God’s presence can shape your requests without making fear disappear at once.
days.reflectionQuestion: What does the psalmist seek while afraid, and what does that reveal about your own deepest requests?
days.prayerPrompt: Tell God what you fear and what you most desire from Him as you wait.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord, meet me in my fear and teach me to seek Your presence. Give me courage to wait for You without hiding my questions. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Receive Scripture’s work
days.devotional: Scripture equips God’s people for good work through more than information. Allow its correction and training to shape your response to Christ.
days.reflectionQuestion: Which part of Scripture’s work—teaching, correction, or training—do you most readily receive, and which do you resist?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God to help you welcome the teaching or correction in Scripture that you find difficult to receive.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, make me teachable before Your Word. Correct what needs to change and prepare me to do good with humility. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Learn to recognize Jesus
days.devotional: Jesus meets disappointed disciples and opens the Scriptures to them. Their expectations need to be reshaped by the suffering and glory of the Messiah.
days.reflectionQuestion: How might your expectations of Jesus need to change as you learn to understand Scripture in relation to Him?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring an expectation of Jesus that has disappointed you, and ask Him to deepen your understanding through Scripture.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, open my understanding as I read. Help me recognize You even when Your way challenges what I expected. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Remember His words
days.devotional: The psalmist speaks of seeking, remembering, declaring, and delighting. Choose a way of returning to Scripture that gives its words room in ordinary life.
days.reflectionQuestion: What could help God’s Word become something you remember and delight in, rather than only something you finish reading?
days.prayerPrompt: Choose a phrase from today’s reading to return to in prayer, asking God to help you remember and practice it.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, give me delight in Your Word. Help me remember what I read and carry it into the ordinary choices of this day. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Seek understanding together
days.devotional: The people listen as God’s instruction is explained. Understanding leads to a response that includes shared joy and care for those who have nothing prepared.
days.reflectionQuestion: What do you learn from a community that seeks understanding and responds with both tears and joy?
days.prayerPrompt: Pray for understanding of Scripture and for a generous response to the people who share life with you.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord, help us listen to Your Word together. Let understanding lead us to honest repentance, shared joy, and care for one another. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Make room to receive
days.devotional: Jesus describes pressures that prevent the word from bearing fruit. Notice the worries and desires competing for your attention without assuming a quick response is lasting growth.
days.reflectionQuestion: What currently competes with your ability to receive God’s Word and respond over time?
days.prayerPrompt: Name a worry or desire that crowds out attention to God, and ask for help making room to listen.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, show me what competes with Your words in my life. Give me a receptive heart and patience for growth that takes time. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Put the word into practice
days.devotional: James connects receiving the word with changed speech and practical care. Consider one place where listening needs to become action.
days.reflectionQuestion: Where might hearing the truth have become a substitute for practicing it?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God to show you one place where listening needs to become a change in speech or practical care.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, help me do more than agree with what I hear. Guide my words and actions toward the care Your Word calls for. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Build on Jesus’ teaching
days.devotional: Both builders hear, but only one acts on Jesus’ words. The difference appears under pressure, when admiration alone cannot provide a foundation.
days.reflectionQuestion: What teaching of Jesus needs to become a decision, habit, or action rather than an admired idea?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring one teaching of Jesus into prayer and ask for courage to put it into practice.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, help me build my life on Your words. Give me courage to obey in the decisions I face today. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Pray to your Father
days.devotional: Jesus directs prayer away from performance and toward the Father. His model makes room for God’s purposes, daily need, forgiveness, and help against evil.
days.reflectionQuestion: How would your prayer change if you were more aware of your Father than of how your words sound?
days.prayerPrompt: Pray slowly about God’s purposes, your daily needs, forgiveness, and the help you need against temptation.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, You know my needs before I speak. Teach me to seek Your purposes, receive daily provision, and extend the forgiveness I need myself. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Bring an honest lament
days.devotional: The psalmist asks how long and still addresses God. Honest lament can remain an act of relationship when relief has not arrived.
days.reflectionQuestion: What unresolved grief or frustration could you bring to God without first making it sound acceptable?
days.prayerPrompt: Tell God honestly what feels unresolved, without trying to make your grief sound more acceptable.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord, I do not know how long this sorrow will last. Hear my questions and help me keep bringing my heart to You. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Ask for help
days.devotional: Jesus encourages His disciples to ask and points them to the Father’s goodness. Dependence grows as you bring actual needs rather than trying to become self-sufficient first.
days.reflectionQuestion: What does Jesus’ description of the Father invite you to expect when you ask for help?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask the Father for the help you need, remembering the goodness Jesus describes.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, help me come to You with honest requests. Give me Your Spirit’s help and teach me to trust Your care. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Approach with confidence
days.devotional: Jesus’ sympathy gives weak people reason to approach God for mercy and help. Your need is a reason to come, not a requirement to stay away.
days.reflectionQuestion: What weakness are you reluctant to bring to God, and how does Jesus’ compassion address that reluctance?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring a weakness you tend to conceal, asking Jesus for mercy and help.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, You understand weakness. Help me approach You honestly and receive the mercy and grace I need today. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Bring specific concerns
days.devotional: Paul joins prayer and thanksgiving with attention and practice. Bring your concerns honestly, and consider what you are repeatedly allowing to occupy your thoughts.
days.reflectionQuestion: How can you bring specific concerns to God while also practicing gratitude and attending to what is good?
days.prayerPrompt: Name a specific concern and a specific reason for gratitude, bringing both to God.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, I bring You the concerns occupying my mind. Thank You for the good I can still name; guide my thoughts and actions in Your peace. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Receive help in weakness
days.devotional: Creation and believers groan as they await renewal. The Spirit’s help means that difficulty finding words does not leave you alone before God.
days.reflectionQuestion: What hope does the Spirit’s help offer when you do not know what to pray?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask the Spirit for help in a concern you do not know how to express.
days.writtenPrayer: Holy Spirit, help me where my words run out. Sustain my hope while I wait for the renewal God has promised. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Entrust the outcome
days.devotional: Jesus speaks honestly about the suffering before Him and yields to the Father. Surrender need not conceal anguish or make a painful desire sound easy.
days.reflectionQuestion: Can you tell God what you truly desire while also entrusting the outcome to Him?
days.prayerPrompt: Tell the Father what you deeply desire, and ask for help entrusting the outcome to Him.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, You know what I want and what I fear. Help me be honest with You and trust You when obedience is painful. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Return to the Father
days.devotional: Jesus’ story exposes both open wandering and resentful obedience. Consider how the father’s welcome challenges the way you imagine returning to God.
days.reflectionQuestion: Which son’s attitude do you recognize in yourself, and what surprises you about the father’s response?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God to expose both wandering and resentment, and help you receive His welcome.
days.writtenPrayer: Merciful Father, I recognize myself in both sons. Help me return to You and rejoice when Your mercy welcomes others. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Ask for a renewed heart
days.devotional: This prayer moves beyond escaping consequences to asking for cleansing and a renewed heart. Confession names wrongdoing while depending on God’s mercy.
days.reflectionQuestion: Are you asking only for consequences to change, or also for your desires and motives to be renewed?
days.prayerPrompt: Confess a wrongdoing plainly, asking God to renew the desires beneath it.
days.writtenPrayer: Merciful God, forgive my sin and renew my heart. Help me seek more than relief from consequences; teach me a different way to live. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Depend on God’s renewal
days.devotional: God promises cleansing and a new heart to His people. The passage directs attention to His initiative and Spirit rather than their ability to repair themselves alone.
days.reflectionQuestion: What does God’s promise to renew His people reveal about the limits of self-reform and the need for His Spirit?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God for the renewal that you cannot produce through determination alone.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord, I cannot remake my heart by willpower alone. Cleanse me and shape my desires by Your Spirit. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Live in freedom from sin
days.devotional: Paul grounds a new way of living in union with Christ’s death and resurrection. Grace invites active resistance to sin rather than resignation to its rule.
days.reflectionQuestion: What changes when you approach sin as something you need not obey rather than something that defines you?
days.prayerPrompt: Name a sinful pattern you have treated as inevitable, and ask for help resisting it in Christ.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for the new life You give. Help me turn away from sin and offer myself to God today. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Let mercy reshape your thinking
days.devotional: Paul appeals to God’s mercy before calling for transformed living. Bring your ordinary choices and inherited assumptions into that response of worship.
days.reflectionQuestion: Which assumptions about success, worth, or happiness need to be examined in light of God’s mercy?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring an assumption about success or worth before God and ask how His mercy should reshape it.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, renew my thinking through Your mercy. Help me offer You my ordinary life with a willing heart. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Practice a different response
days.devotional: Putting away the old life includes learning truthful, generous, and forgiving habits. Renewal becomes visible in the way people speak and respond to one another.
days.reflectionQuestion: What harmful pattern needs to be replaced with a specific, constructive way of treating others?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God for a constructive response to replace a harmful habit in your speech or relationships.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, show me what I need to put away and what I need to practice instead. Make my words truthful, generous, and forgiving. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Walk by the Spirit
days.devotional: Paul contrasts destructive desires with the fruit of the Spirit. Consider the character of your relationships as you ask for help to walk with Him.
days.reflectionQuestion: Which qualities named here are developing in you, and where do you need greater dependence on the Spirit?
days.prayerPrompt: Pray about one quality of the Spirit’s fruit that is needed in your relationships today.
days.writtenPrayer: Holy Spirit, grow Your fruit in the way I treat people. Help me respond with love and self-control when my desires pull elsewhere. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Receive grace and walk in it
days.devotional: Good works follow God’s gracious action in Christ. They are a response to being made alive, never a price paid for acceptance.
days.reflectionQuestion: How does being saved by grace change the place of good works in your life?
days.prayerPrompt: Thank God for grace, and ask Him to help you serve from gratitude rather than a need to earn acceptance.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, thank You for saving by grace through Christ. Let the good I do flow from gratitude for what You have given. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Receive belonging
days.devotional: John describes belonging to God as a gift received through Christ. Consider how that welcome changes the weight you give to other people’s approval.
days.reflectionQuestion: What does receiving the right to become God’s child offer that approval from other people cannot?
days.prayerPrompt: Tell God where you are seeking approval, and ask for help receiving belonging through Christ.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, help me receive the welcome You give through Jesus. Let belonging to You shape how I respond to the approval of others. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Live as God’s child
days.devotional: Paul speaks of freedom from condemnation and the Spirit’s witness to adoption. Bring the fears that shape your decisions into this account of life in Christ.
days.reflectionQuestion: Where are you living as though condemnation or fear has the final authority over you?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring a fear of condemnation to God, asking the Spirit to help you live as His child.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, help me receive the freedom found in Christ. Teach me to turn to You as Your child when fear rises. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Belong to His family
days.devotional: Paul describes a movement from slavery to belonging as children and heirs. Receive this relationship as God’s gift rather than a status you must continually purchase.
days.reflectionQuestion: How would life as God’s child differ from continually trying to earn a place in His family?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God to show you where you are living as though your place in His family must be earned.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, thank You for receiving me through Your Son. Help me live in the freedom of belonging to You. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Belong to God’s people
days.devotional: Peter describes a people formed around Christ to declare God’s goodness. Belonging gives you a place among others and a purpose beyond protecting your own standing.
days.reflectionQuestion: How does belonging to God’s people give you both dignity and responsibility?
days.prayerPrompt: Thank God for a place among His people, and ask how you can use it to declare His goodness.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for bringing me into Your people. Help me receive that dignity and use my life to point toward Your goodness. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Find your confidence in Christ
days.devotional: Paul reconsiders the credentials that once defined his confidence. Knowing Christ changes how he values the things that once secured his status.
days.reflectionQuestion: Which accomplishments, credentials, or moral achievements are you tempted to rely on instead of Christ?
days.prayerPrompt: Name a credential or achievement you rely on for worth, and ask Christ to become your deeper confidence.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, You are worth more than the things I use to establish myself. Help me place my confidence in You. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Receive the Father’s love
days.devotional: John begins with the Father’s love and looks toward a future not yet fully seen. Hope in Christ can shape present living without pretending growth is already complete.
days.reflectionQuestion: How might being loved as God’s child shape both your confidence today and your hope for who you will become?
days.prayerPrompt: Thank the Father for His love, and bring your unfinished growth to Him with hope.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, thank You for loving me as Your child. Shape who I am becoming and help me live with hope today. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Love God wholeheartedly
days.devotional: Jesus holds love of God and neighbor together. Consider how devotion to God takes form in the choices you make with your attention, strength, and care.
days.reflectionQuestion: What would wholehearted love of God change about one ordinary decision you face today?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God what wholehearted love would look like in one ordinary choice today.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord, help me love You with my whole life. Guide my attention, strength, and choices toward love of You and my neighbor. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Love because God loved first
days.devotional: John roots Christian love in God’s action toward us. Receiving His love challenges the assumption that another person must first deserve your care.
days.reflectionQuestion: How does being loved first change your response to someone who has not earned your affection?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring someone you find difficult to love before God, remembering His love toward you.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, You loved us first. Help me receive Your love and seek another person’s good without requiring them to earn my care. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Seek a friend’s good
days.devotional: Jesus commands His friends to love in the pattern of His own love. Friendship includes willing another person’s good when it asks something of you.
days.reflectionQuestion: What might it cost to seek a friend’s good rather than merely enjoy their company?
days.prayerPrompt: Pray for a friend’s good and ask Jesus what loving that friend may require of you.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, teach me to love my friends with more than pleasant words. Make me willing to give time and care when it costs me something. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Become a neighbor
days.devotional: Jesus’ story turns attention from defining the limits of obligation to showing mercy. Notice the person whose need interrupts your preferred route through the day.
days.reflectionQuestion: Whose need are you tempted to treat as someone else’s responsibility?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God to draw your attention to a nearby need you have been passing by.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, open my eyes to the person I would rather overlook. Give me compassion and wisdom to respond with practical mercy. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Pray for an enemy
days.devotional: Jesus calls His followers to love beyond the circle of those who love them back. Prayer for an enemy can seek their good while still telling the truth about harm.
days.reflectionQuestion: What could seeking an enemy’s good look like without pretending their wrongdoing is acceptable?
days.prayerPrompt: Pray for an enemy’s good while speaking honestly to God about the harm involved.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, help me seek good even for those who oppose me. Keep my love truthful, and give me wisdom about safe and faithful boundaries. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Let love shape your actions
days.devotional: Paul places love above impressive gifts and achievements. Examine the patience, kindness, and truthfulness of your actions rather than relying only on good intentions.
days.reflectionQuestion: Which description of love most exposes a difference between your intentions and your behavior?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God to expose the gap between your intentions and the patience or kindness people experience from you.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord, let love shape the way I speak and act. Help me become patient and kind when good intentions alone are not enough. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Love through practical care
days.devotional: John connects Christ’s self-giving love with care for a person in need. Consider what you can share in practice, within your actual means.
days.reflectionQuestion: What material need near you could be met through action rather than sympathetic words alone?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring a material need to God and ask what you can share within your actual means.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, keep my compassion from stopping at words. Show me a practical way to share what I have with someone in need. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Choose service over status
days.devotional: Jesus answers a request for prominence by teaching a different understanding of greatness. His own service challenges the desire to place others beneath you.
days.reflectionQuestion: Are you more concerned with being useful to others or being recognized as important?
days.prayerPrompt: Tell Jesus where you desire recognition and ask Him to reshape your understanding of greatness.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, free me from using service to make myself important. Teach me to seek another person’s good with humility. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Serve in ordinary ways
days.devotional: Jesus washes His disciples’ feet with full awareness of who He is. Secure identity and humble service belong together in His example.
days.reflectionQuestion: What ordinary task would you consider beneath you, and how does Jesus’ example challenge that judgment?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask Jesus for willingness to do a useful task you normally avoid or consider beneath you.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, Your humble service challenges my pride. Help me care for others through the ordinary tasks before me. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Consider another person’s interests
days.devotional: Paul points to Christ’s humility as the pattern for shared life. Consider where rivalry or the need for recognition is making it difficult to serve.
days.reflectionQuestion: Where could you consider another person’s interests without insisting on your own status or advantage?
days.prayerPrompt: Pray about a situation where insisting on status prevents you from considering another person’s needs.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, shape my attitude by Your humility. Help me consider others without continually defending my own advantage. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Use the gift you have
days.devotional: Different gifts serve one body. Honest judgment about your abilities can free you to contribute without making another person’s role a measure of your worth.
days.reflectionQuestion: What ability could you use faithfully without comparing its visibility or importance with someone else’s?
days.prayerPrompt: Thank God for an ability you can offer, and ask for freedom from comparison.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, thank You for the gifts entrusted to me. Help me use them faithfully without measuring my worth against someone else’s role. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Serve with God’s strength
days.devotional: Peter joins hospitality and service with dependence on God’s provision. Offer what has been entrusted to you without imagining every need rests on your shoulders.
days.reflectionQuestion: How can you serve with what God supplies rather than treating yourself as the source of everything others need?
days.prayerPrompt: Name the limits you face in service and ask God for strength to offer what He supplies.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord, help me serve with what You provide. Give me humility to accept my limits and receive help from others. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Welcome without repayment
days.devotional: Jesus challenges both the pursuit of honor and invitations designed for return favors. Consider whose company or needs you overlook because they offer no advantage.
days.reflectionQuestion: Who could you welcome or help without expecting repayment, influence, or social benefit?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God whom you could welcome or help without expecting a return.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, broaden my welcome beyond those who can repay me. Help me offer care freely and notice people without social advantage. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Bring the need to Jesus
days.devotional: Jesus responds with compassion to the crowd and involves His disciples in feeding them. Their limited resources are brought into His care rather than treated as the end of the conversation.
days.reflectionQuestion: What do the disciples’ limited resources and Jesus’ provision teach you about bringing an actual need to Him?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring an actual need and your limited resources to Jesus, asking what faithful participation looks like.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, I bring You what I have and the need before me. Give me compassion and wisdom to take the part that is mine. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Receive the world as God’s
days.devotional: The psalm begins by placing the earth and its inhabitants under God’s ownership. Stewardship begins with receiving responsibility for what was never ultimately ours to possess.
days.reflectionQuestion: What changes about ownership when you begin with the conviction that the world belongs to God?
days.prayerPrompt: Thank God for something you tend to call your own and ask how to care for it responsibly.
days.writtenPrayer: Creator God, the world belongs to You. Help me receive what I have with gratitude and care for it as a trust. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Seek lasting treasure
days.devotional: Jesus connects treasure, allegiance, and anxiety. Consider how seeking the Father’s kingdom might reshape one practical decision about provision.
days.reflectionQuestion: What do your spending, saving, and recurring worries suggest about where you seek security?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring a financial worry or desire for security to the Father, asking for wisdom to seek His kingdom.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, You know my needs. Help me place my hope in You and make wise choices about what I treasure. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Be rich toward God
days.devotional: The rich man plans for abundance without reckoning with the limits of his life. Jesus invites a deeper account of security than having more stored away.
days.reflectionQuestion: What would make your life rich toward God rather than merely well supplied?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God to reveal where accumulation has become a substitute for a life directed toward Him.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, keep abundance from becoming my definition of life. Teach me generosity and help me become rich toward You. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Act faithfully with what is entrusted
days.devotional: Jesus’ parable asks how servants respond to what has been entrusted to them. Consider whether fear is preventing responsible action in a task you already have.
days.reflectionQuestion: What responsibility have you neglected because of fear, and what would faithful action look like?
days.prayerPrompt: Name a neglected responsibility and ask for courage to take a small, responsible step.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord, help me act faithfully with what has been entrusted to me. Give me wisdom and courage where fear has kept me inactive. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Give attention wisely
days.devotional: Paul calls believers to live wisely, with gratitude and attention to God’s will. Notice how repeated uses of time are shaping your life with others.
days.reflectionQuestion: Which recurring use of your time or attention is inconsistent with living thoughtfully before God?
days.prayerPrompt: Pray about one recurring use of your time or attention that needs to change.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, teach me to use my days thoughtfully. Help me give attention to what honors You and serves the people around me. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Give freely
days.devotional: Paul connects willing generosity with thanksgiving to God and provision for others. Giving is an opportunity to share, not a way to purchase praise or guaranteed wealth.
days.reflectionQuestion: How could you give freely without using generosity to seek approval or guarantee financial gain?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God to make your giving willing and free from the desire for praise or guaranteed reward.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, thank You for what You provide. Give me a willing heart to share and let my generosity lead to thanksgiving. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Practice contentment and generosity
days.devotional: Paul warns against putting hope in uncertain riches. Contentment and readiness to share can shape your life at the level of resources you actually have.
days.reflectionQuestion: What would contentment, generosity, and hope in God look like at your present level of income?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring your present resources to God and ask for contentment, wisdom, and readiness to share.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord, guard my heart from the love of money. Teach me contentment and generosity with the resources I have today. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Make room for shared life
days.devotional: The believers’ shared life includes worship, learning, meals, and material care. Consider which part of that life requires deliberate space in your week.
days.reflectionQuestion: Which part of shared Christian life needs more space in your schedule: learning, fellowship, meals, prayer, or practical care?
days.prayerPrompt: Pray about one way you can make room for learning, prayer, meals, or practical care with other Christians.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, help me make room for shared life with Your people. Teach me to receive care and contribute to the care of others. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Welcome those Christ brings near
days.devotional: Paul describes Christ bringing divided people into one household. Remembering His work challenges the barriers believers maintain against one another.
days.reflectionQuestion: Which divisions are you treating as permanent that Christ calls His people to overcome?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring a division among believers to Christ, asking how you can respond to His reconciling work.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, You bring people near through Your peace. Help me stop treating divisions You challenge as barriers I must defend. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Receive your place in the body
days.devotional: The body needs its different members, including those easily overlooked. Both superiority and withdrawal obscure the interdependence Paul describes.
days.reflectionQuestion: Where do you act as though you do not need others—or as though the community does not need you?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God to show you where you need others and where you can contribute to the body of Christ.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, thank You for giving us different gifts and needs. Help me receive my place among Your people with humility. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Help one another grow
days.devotional: Christ equips His people to build up the body in love. Growth involves receiving help and contributing to the maturity of others.
days.reflectionQuestion: How could you contribute to another person’s maturity rather than only seek your own encouragement?
days.prayerPrompt: Pray for one person’s growth in Christ, and ask how you can support it.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, help me build others up in love. Give me patience to grow alongside them and humility to receive their help. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Practice a shared life of grace
days.devotional: Paul describes compassion, patience, forgiveness, and love as the clothing of a people loved by God. Consider the atmosphere your own words help create.
days.reflectionQuestion: Which quality named here would most change the atmosphere of a community you belong to?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God to shape the atmosphere you create through your words, patience, and forgiveness.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, clothe me with compassion and patience. Let the way I speak help make room for peace and gratitude among Your people. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Encourage love and good works
days.devotional: Confidence to approach God is joined with responsibility to encourage one another. Think about a specific person whose faithful action you can help sustain.
days.reflectionQuestion: What would intentional encouragement toward love and good works look like in one of your relationships?
days.prayerPrompt: Name someone who needs encouragement toward love and good works, and pray for a thoughtful response.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord, help me notice when another person needs encouragement. Give me words and actions that strengthen their hope in You. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Carry burdens humbly
days.devotional: Paul calls for gentle restoration and shared burdens while warning against self-deception. Help can be truthful without becoming superior or harsh.
days.reflectionQuestion: How can you help someone with a struggle while remaining humble about your own vulnerability?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring someone’s struggle to God while acknowledging your own need for grace.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, teach me to carry burdens with humility. Help me offer gentle, truthful care and remember my own need for mercy. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Go with Jesus’ presence
days.devotional: Jesus sends His disciples under His authority and promises His presence. The task includes teaching a life of obedience, not merely gaining agreement.
days.reflectionQuestion: How do Jesus’ authority and continuing presence change the way you understand the task of making disciples?
days.prayerPrompt: Pray about the people and places where Jesus calls you to witness, remembering His continuing presence.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, help me follow Your sending with confidence in Your authority. Teach me to point others toward a life of obedience to You. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Receive His sending
days.devotional: Jesus meets fearful disciples with peace and sends them. Witness begins with receiving from Him before assuming the burden of speaking for Him.
days.reflectionQuestion: What changes when you understand witness as something Jesus sends and equips you to do, not something you undertake alone?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring your fear about speaking of Jesus to Him and ask for His peace and help.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, meet me in my fear with Your peace. Help me receive what You give and respond faithfully where You send me. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Depend on the Spirit
days.devotional: Jesus directs His followers toward the Spirit’s power and their calling as witnesses. Their task is grounded in His promise rather than control over every outcome.
days.reflectionQuestion: Where do you need dependence on the Spirit rather than greater confidence in your own persuasive ability?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask the Spirit to help you witness to Jesus without making persuasive ability your source of confidence.
days.writtenPrayer: Holy Spirit, help me bear witness to Jesus with honesty and courage. Teach me to depend on You rather than control the outcome. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Direct attention to God
days.devotional: Jesus describes a visible life whose good works lead others to glorify the Father. Consider the difference between helpful visibility and a search for admiration.
days.reflectionQuestion: How can your visible actions direct attention toward God rather than toward your own goodness?
days.prayerPrompt: Pray that your visible actions would help others recognize the Father’s goodness.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, let the good I do point toward You. Keep me from turning service into a display of my own importance. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Speak with grace
days.devotional: Paul joins prayer for open doors with wise conduct and gracious speech. Listening and thoughtful timing can be part of faithful witness.
days.reflectionQuestion: How could prayer, wise timing, and gracious speech change a conversation about faith?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask God for an open opportunity, patient listening, and gracious words in a conversation about faith.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, guide my conversations with wisdom. Help me listen carefully and speak of Jesus with grace and clarity. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Explain hope with gentleness
days.devotional: Peter calls believers to be ready to explain their hope with gentleness and respect. The manner of speaking belongs with the message, even under pressure.
days.reflectionQuestion: Could someone who disagrees with you still recognize gentleness and respect in the way you explain your hope?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring someone who disagrees with you to God and ask for gentleness in explaining your hope.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, help me speak of my hope with respect. Let my conduct reflect Your goodness even when the conversation is difficult. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Let Christ’s love shape your witness
days.devotional: Paul describes Christ’s love as the reason for a new way of seeing and living. The message of reconciliation invites motives shaped by that love.
days.reflectionQuestion: How does Christ’s reconciling love change your motives for speaking to others about Him?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask Christ to let His reconciling love shape your motives for speaking about Him.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, let Your love direct the way I see people. Help me speak of reconciliation with the humility of someone who has received mercy. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Consider Jesus when weary
days.devotional: Hebrews calls believers to endure with their attention on Jesus. Name what hinders you while remembering the One whose endurance gives this call its center.
days.reflectionQuestion: What is hindering your faithfulness, and how does considering Jesus change your response to weariness?
days.prayerPrompt: Name what is hindering you and ask Jesus to sustain you in weariness.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, help me keep my attention on You when I am tired. Give me courage to lay aside what hinders me and continue with trust. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Ask for wisdom in difficulty
days.devotional: James directs people facing trials to ask God for wisdom. Endurance does not require already knowing how to respond to every difficulty.
days.reflectionQuestion: What wisdom do you need to ask God for in a difficulty you cannot quickly remove?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring a difficulty you cannot quickly solve to God and ask for the wisdom needed today.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, I need wisdom for what I cannot easily change. Help me respond with trust and grow in endurance as I depend on You. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Acknowledge weakness with hope
days.devotional: Paul describes fragile servants carrying a treasure that comes from God. Weakness and suffering are real, but they do not exhaust the account of what God is doing.
days.reflectionQuestion: How can you acknowledge real weakness without concluding that God has stopped working?
days.prayerPrompt: Tell God honestly where you feel weak, and ask Him to renew your hope.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, I feel the limits of my strength. Help me remember that Your work does not depend on pretending to be unbreakable. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Receive peace amid trouble
days.devotional: Jesus prepares His disciples for sorrow and trouble while directing them to peace in Him. Hope rests on His victory rather than a promise of painless circumstances.
days.reflectionQuestion: What does Jesus actually promise amid trouble, and how does that differ from expecting a trouble-free life?
days.prayerPrompt: Bring a present trouble to Jesus and ask for the peace He offers within it.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, You did not promise a life without trouble. Help me receive peace in You and remember Your victory when I am afraid. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Continue toward Christ
days.devotional: Paul openly says that he has not arrived and continues toward Christ. You can acknowledge an unfinished life while taking the next faithful step.
days.reflectionQuestion: What would continued pursuit of Christ look like without either denying past failures or remaining defined by them?
days.prayerPrompt: Ask Christ for help taking the next faithful step without denying or being trapped by your past.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord Jesus, I have not arrived, and I still need Your grace. Help me keep pursuing You with honesty about the past and hope for what lies ahead. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Rest in inseparable love
days.devotional: Paul names hardship rather than denying it, then declares the strength of God’s love in Christ. Bring a particular fear into that assurance.
days.reflectionQuestion: Which fear is challenged by the assurance that suffering cannot separate you from God’s love in Christ?
days.prayerPrompt: Name a fear of being abandoned by God and bring it before His love in Christ.
days.writtenPrayer: Father, hold my hope steady in Your love. Help me trust that suffering cannot separate me from You in Christ Jesus. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.

days.title: Continue beyond these 77 days
days.devotional: Jude calls believers to prayer, mercy, and life in God’s love, and closes with praise to the One able to keep them. Completing these days is an invitation to continue depending on Him.
days.reflectionQuestion: Which practices will help you continue after this study, and whose power ultimately gives you confidence?
days.prayerPrompt: Thank God for these 77 days and ask which practices to continue in dependence on Him.
days.writtenPrayer: Lord, thank You for meeting me through these days. Help me continue in prayer, mercy, and Your love, trusting Your power to keep me. Amen.
days.intentionInvitation: Choose one practical response to today’s reading.
